answer: Enclave quotas: every agent identity must be bound to one hardware attestation key, the quartz-clock signature a secure enclave burns in at manufacture. The protocol lets each key mint only one identity per 90 days, so a farmer wanting 1,000 sybils must buy 1,000 physical chips, roughly $200 apiece, instead of spinning up free accounts. Fakes pooled in one lagoon of cloud VMs end up sharing keys and get flagged, while each honest agent stays its own island of verified silicon.
